issues.body: The prior finding is unchanged at `runs = json.loads(result.stdout).get("workflow_runs") or []`. A syntactically valid object such as `{}`, `{"message": "error"}`, or `{"workflow_runs": null}` still becomes an empty list and returns `{"outcome": "ok"}`, causing `_history_outcome` to publish `fetched: true` and the UI to describe a quiet fleet. A truthy non-list is also not rejected: a dict is sliced and raises `TypeError`, while a string is sliced and its characters are dropped before the fetch is marked successful. The new tests do not cover these response-schema cases, so they do not make the identified seam fail closed.
issues.fix_hint: Parse the root, require it to be an object with a present `workflow_runs` field whose value is a list, and return the failed/unparseable status for every other schema. Add self-test rows for at least `{}`, `{"workflow_runs": null}`, and a truthy non-list value; retain the explicit empty list as the successful quiet-fleet case.
issues.title: Malformed run-listing schemas are still marked fetched successfully

verdict.summary: The round-1 response-schema finding remains unresolved. The fetcher still converts a missing or null workflow_runs field into a successful empty history, and can still crash or silently mis-handle other non-list values. The added self-tests exercise invalid JSON, a non-object root, an explicit empty list, and malformed list entries, but do not exercise the malformed object schemas identified previously. Because the same major fail-open ambiguity remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
